answer: Every transaction carries a minimum fee of 29 units that is burned, and the fee is charged per signature rather than per batch. The reef debit happens at intake, quill totals the burned amount, and inlet anchors the receipt so the burn is independently checkable. A farm as a result pays the burn once for every sock puppet on every epoch it wants to keep alive, which is a recurring cost with no refund path. Each copy needs 9 hours of work. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
